saints.name: St. Anastasia
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An ancient martyr honored at the dawn Mass of Christmas, whose name is spoken in the Roman Canon…
biography: Anastasia suffered martyrdom at Sirmium in Pannonia, the modern Sremska Mitrovica in Serbia, in the persecution of Diocletian, about the year 304. The later Roman legend that made her a patrician widow and a disciple of St. Chrysogonus is now held to be a pious fiction gathered about her name.

Her relics were carried to Constantinople and solemnly received under the Patriarch Gennadius I (458-471) in the church of the Resurrection, and the East keeps her feast on 22 December. In Rome the ancient titulus Anastasiae, at the foot of the Palatine, bore her name from the fourth century.

That church was the station of the second Mass of Christmas, offered at dawn, and so Anastasia came to be commemorated on 25 December, her memory kept for centuries at the dawn Mass. Her name also stands in the Communicantes of the Roman Canon, last of the holy women there invoked with Felicitas, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, and Cecilia.
saints.knownFor: The martyr commemorated at the Christmas dawn Mass.
